rows: I recognise your mastery of ground work. You must nevertheless demonstrate a legal takedown before it becomes relevant.
A strike may score an advantage. It does not automatically constitute a fall.
A wrestler in flight has committed to a trajectory. The examination is in the landing.
Controlling tempo is legitimate. Delaying the contest is not. I will oblige you to engage.
A paying spectator deserves a complete contest. Both participants bear that obligation.
I prefer a demonstration to a lecture. Watch the opening exchange.
A programme's running order is not a measure of wrestling quality. Our match will establish the standard.
Observe my stance. You will have to solve it.
The takedown is a problem in two stages. You have dealt with neither yet.
A strike can change the course of a contest. Let me demonstrate that principle.
First establish your position beneath the trajectory. Then tell me how simple it is.
A pause within an exchange is not the same as a delay outside it.
Quite right. Let us meet the obligation in full.
A claim to precedence is not a sporting result.
You have identified {strength}. My task is to formulate and demonstrate the correct response.
I have made your {strength} the question. The answer will be a matter of application.
The disagreement is sporting, not personal. My intention is to win the contest.
There is no benefit in raising one's voice. The bell will suffice.
A loud argument is not a more accurate one.
One fall, contested by two participants only. A perfectly reasonable proposition.
Let us examine your claim on the mat, under wrestling conditions.
Remain on the canvas for the test. No recourse to the ropes for flight.
Remain within the designated contest area. That is where we settle this.
Agreed. The outcome is the outstanding question.
Return to the original question. You have not addressed it.
That point is valid. I accept it.
Then we have resolved that matter.
The examination will be demanding. I intend to pass it by winning.
One clean fall, in the centre of the ring. No qualification.
I have a method in mind. Demonstration will be more useful than description.
I cannot establish the proposition with the information I have. The allegation should therefore be withdrawn.
You are entitled to a demonstration of the facts. I cannot provide one in support of that assertion.
Then the unsupported proposition has no further place in our exchange. The contest remains.
A reasonable distinction. We can test the wrestling without relying on an unverified claim.
A successful hold, its escape and the resulting position. Each can be observed independently.
The legal fall will establish the result. It cannot establish an allegation about your character.
Let us distinguish the allegation from the contest. What can a properly officiated match establish?
What observation in the ring would justify the conclusion you wish us to draw?
Your proposed response to my {strength} requires successful application under resistance. That remains to be demonstrated.
By identifying my {strength}, you have completed the first stage of the examination. The second begins at the bell.
